text:
sre-bot: [ALERT] target-group edge-models-prod has high unhealthy hosts (80%) - repeated 5xx and healthcheck timeouts starting 12:03 UTC. metrics: https://grafana/redwood/alerts/edge-models

maria: seeing it too, ALB says healthcheck failures. Investigating.

liam: jumpbox -> `curl -v http://10.10.34.56:8080/health` -> `* Connection timed out` but pod is Running and process listening (`ss -ltnp` shows 0.0.0.0:8080).

maria: did a tcpdump on eni-0a1b2c3d (edge-subnet-3) and I can see SYNs from ALB IPs reaching node, but no SYN-ACK leaving the node back to the LB.

anya: NACLs are stateless — you need both directions. If inbound 80/8080 is allowed but ephemeral return ports are denied, replies get dropped. Could be our recent NACL tighten.

liam: confirmed NACL `nacl-0f9e8d7c` on us-west2-edge-subnet-3 has DENY for port range 32768-65535 (rule 130) and it was applied after the cleanup job earlier today. inbound still allows 8080 but the egress ephemeral deny would block the LB's ephemeral source ports on the return flow.

owen: that cleanup job erroneously targeted all edge subnets; edge-subnet-3 contains ENIs used by gpu nodes (model-serving). Looks like a mis-tagging filter in the job.

maria: quick mitigation: add allow rules for ephemeral range both directions on the NACLs for all edge subnets, and scope more carefully. Long term: avoid NACL-wide cleanup for edge subnets or use SGs referencing LB SG (stateful).

liam: applying hotfix via CLI now. command:
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0f9e8d7c --rule-number 120 --protocol tcp --port-range From=32768,To=65535 --egress false --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0f9e8d7c --rule-number 121 --protocol tcp --port-range From=32768,To=65535 --egress true --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
```
liam: terraform plan -> applied (change set id: cs-12345). ETA ~8m for propagation.

sre-bot: [AUTO] terraform apply started by liam at 12:18 UTC (run-id: tf-run-77).

maria: after the change I see SYN-ACKs returning and ALB target group healthy count climbing. Manual curl from jumpbox now returns `ok`.

anya: opened INC-9876 and assigned to infra-team to add a guard in the NACL cleanup job so it ignores subnets tagged `edge=gpu` and so it requires manual review for anything hitting 100+ ENIs.

owen: follow-up action items: 1) add integration test that simulates ALB healthcheck through NACLs for edge subnets, 2) change NACL cleanup to skip `edge-*` CIDR blocks, 3) add runbook step to prefer SG-based protections for ALBs when possible.

liam: rolling a small config test to prod pipeline to catch this. :thumbsup:

maria: closing alert, will keep monitoring for 30m. thanks team.
